lina: hi all, brand new here! trying to run the sample app locally but postgres container fails with permission denied creating /var/lib/postgresql/data. compose snippet is a simple host bind: `./pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data` and `POSTGRES_PASSWORD=postgres`. i'm on macOS (Docker Desktop, M1). after some tries i also hit `FATAL: password authentication failed for user "postgres"`. any rapid checklist for newbies?

.tom: welcome Lina! :wave: short checklist that fixes 90% of these cases:
1) Host-mounted dirs on mac often have wrong owner for the postgres uid used inside the container. The postgres user in the official image usually has uid 999. On your host run: `sudo chown -R 999:999 ./pgdata`.
2) If initdb ran previously with a different UID or password you'll need to reset the local state: `docker-compose down -v` then `rm -rf ./pgdata/*` (only safe for local dev).
3) Easiest fix: switch to a named Docker volume to avoid macOS mount issues. In compose: `volumes:
  pgdata:` and `- pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data`.
4) To confirm the uid the image uses: `docker run --rm postgres:15 id postgres` or `docker run --rm postgres:15 sh -c "getent passwd postgres"`.

rachel: +1 to Tom. Also note Docker Desktop's gRPC-FUSE/osxfs differences can cause odd perms and slowness. If you must keep a host dir, set ownership from inside a container: `docker run --rm -v $(pwd)/pgdata:/host alpine chown -R 999:999 /host`.

devops-bot: onboarding docs updated: added mac M1 notes for Postgres host mounts and a quick recovery recipe. https://redwood-internal/onboarding/local-db :white_check_mark:

lina: did `sudo chown -R 999:999 ./pgdata` and `docker-compose down -v` -> `rm -rf ./pgdata/*` then brought it up and Postgres stayed up. psql now accepts the POSTGRES_PASSWORD. thanks all! one last Q: Redis — should i persist it locally?

.tom: for dev we usually don't persist Redis unless you need state between restarts. `image: redis:7` with `ports: - "6379:6379"` is fine. If you want a persisted instance use a named volume too.

lina: perfect, will update my onboarding notes. thanks :pray:
